summary: Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He succeeded Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1937.

Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Mumbai and Elphinstone College from circa 1864 to 1869, later serving as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Elphinstone College from around 1869 to 1872.

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1914–1945) and Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1945–1976), and he taught Masaaki Hattori.

Kate Crosby is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She held posts at Cardiff University (attested 2002), the Buddhist Institute in 2003, and the Seiyu Kiriyama post at SOAS University of London, teaching David Azzopardi and Jotika Khur-Yearn.
Kate Wharton works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London in 2008 and held a post at Birkbeck, University of London, attested in 2010.
Katharina Sabernig is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Vienna in 2017 and held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at McGill University, where she studied under supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2008).

Katherine Anne Paul works in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. She was supervised for her doctorate by Gudrun Bühnemann and was taught by Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam V. Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones is an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Davidson College and earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, also studying under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (~1968–1970) and McGill University (~1970–1977). She served as Professor at McGill University from around 1978 to 2017 and taught Barbra R. Clayton.

Kathleen D. Morrison is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Notre Dame, the University of New Mexico, and UC Berkeley. She was Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Northwestern University (~1993–1996) and held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

Kathleen M. Erndl was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held posts at DePauw University, University of Wisconsin-Madison, Lewis & Clark College (~1988–1993), and Florida State University as Associate Professor of Religion (~1993–2017), where she taught Cameron Bailey and Lindsay G. McCune.

Kathleen McDonald works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Gyatso, 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (~1974), Ngawang Dhargyey, Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown specializes in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Michigan in 2000 under doctoral supervisor Walter M. Spink and committee members Donald S. Lopez Jr. and John C. Huntington.

Katia Buffetrille is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. She completed her studies, including a PhD, at Paris Nanterre University under Alexander W. Macdonald between roughly 1985 and 1996, and took up a post at École Pratique des Hautes Études around 1997.

Katsuhiko Kamimura was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, and with V. Raghavan. He held posts at Kokugakuin University (~1973–1980) and the University of Tokyo (~1980–2003), and taught Mizuho Okita and Yuko Yokochi.
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University from circa 1964 to 1968 and served as a professor at Hanazono University.

Katsumi Mimaki studied at Kyoto University, INALCO, University of Paris, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held research and professorial posts at Kyoto University from 1976 to 2011 and taught numerous students.

Katsumi Okimoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a graduate student at the University of Tokyo from circa 1968 to 1973. He served at Hanazono University as a professor (~1981–2008) and later as director (~2008).
